typeChecks: __Equal<ReturnType<typeof pluck<{ a: number; b: string }, "a">>, number[]>
title: Generics through mapped types
prompt: Write three functions that work together. `firstOr<T>(items, fallback)` returns the first item when the array is not empty, even if it is 0 or `""`, and `fallback` otherwise. `drafts(articles)` returns `{ id, title }` for each article where `published` is `false`, in order, with no other fields. `pluck<T, K extends keyof T>(items, key)` returns the value of field `key` from each item, typed as `T[K][]`.
hints: Use the array length, not truthiness, to decide whether a first item exists.
Filter unpublished articles, then build new objects with only `id` and `title`.
In `pluck`, `K extends keyof T` limits the key, and `T[K]` is the type of each value.
checks: __same(drafts([{ id: "a", title: "A", published: false, author: "s" }, { id: "b", title: "B", published: true }]), [{ id: "a", title: "A" }])
__same(firstOr(drafts([{ id: "c", title: "", published: false }]), { id: "-", title: "none" }), { id: "c", title: "" })
__same(pluck(drafts([{ id: "a", title: "A", published: false }, { id: "b", title: "B", published: false }]), "title"), ["A", "B"])

wrongAnswers.misconception: Uses `||`, so a first item of 0 is replaced.
Copies every field of each article.

feedback: Use the array length, not truthiness, to decide whether a first item exists.
